content: Dr. Marleen Temmerman serves as the Director of the World Health Organization (WHO) and is based at Avenue Appia 20, 1211 Geneva 27, Switzerland. She oversees the Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases. Professor John Charles Reeder, also a Director at WHO, is located at the same address in Geneva, Switzerland. His expertise includes the development of WHO guidelines, such as the fortification of food-grade salt with iodine to prevent and control iodine deficiency disorders. Ms. Deena Alasfoor, from the Ministry of Health in Muscat, Oman, specializes in health program management, food legislation, and surveillance within primary healthcare systems. Dr. Kalid Asrat Tasew, affiliated with St. Paul Hospital Millennium Medical College in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, focuses on pediatrics and primary healthcare. Dr. Mary Chea, working with the National Nutrition Programme at the National Maternal and Child Health Center in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, is an expert in program implementation and midwifery. Dr. Luz Maria De-Regil, based in Ottawa, Canada, at the Micronutrient Initiative, specializes in epidemiology, systematic reviews, and program implementation. Dr. Heba El Laithy, from the Faculty of Economics at Cairo University in Egypt, has expertise in statistics and economics. Dr. Davina Ghersi, working with the National Health and Medical Research Council in Canberra, Australia, focuses on policy-making, systematic reviews, and evidence-based research. Dr. Maria Elena del Socorro Jefferds, from the Nutrition Branch of the Division of Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Obesity at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, specializes in behavioral science and program evaluation. Dr. Rukhsana Haider, representing the Training and Assistance for Health and Nutrition (TAHN) Foundation in Dhaka, Bangladesh, is an expert in breastfeeding and capacity-building in counseling and nutrition. Dr. Patrick Wilfried Kolsteren, from the Department of Public Health at the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium, focuses on public health, food safety, and laboratory methods. Dr. Guansheng Ma, affiliated with the National Institute for Nutrition and Food Safety at the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention in Beijing, China, specializes in food safety, public health, and program management. Dr. Lynnette Neufeld, working with the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN) in Geneva, Switzerland, has expertise in micronutrients, epidemiology, and program monitoring. Dr. Orishi Ebere Orisakwe, from the Toxicology Unit at the Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Port Harcourt in Nigeria, focuses on pharmacology, food safety, and toxicology. Dr. Mical Paul, based at the Infectious Diseases Unit of Rabin Medical Center and Sackler Faculty of Medicine at Tel Aviv University in Israel, specializes in infectious diseases and HIV. Dr. Juan Pablo Peña-Rosas, Coordinator at the Evidence and Programme Guidance Department of Nutrition for Health and Development at WHO, is a key figure in the development of WHO guidelines. Dr. Lisa Rogers, a Technical Officer in the same department, contributes to evidence-based program guidance. Dr. Nigel Rollins, a Medical Officer in the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health (MCA), focuses on research and development. Ms. Victoria Saint, a Technical Officer in the Department of Public Health, Environmental, and Social Determinants of Health (PHE), specializes in social determinants of health. Dr. Eugenio Villar Montesinos, Coordinator in the same department, also focuses on social determinants of health. Dr. Godfrey Xuereb, a Technical Officer in the Department of Chronic Diseases and Health Promotion, specializes in surveillance and population-based prevention. Mr. Gerardo Zamora, a Consultant in the Evidence and Programme Guidance Department of Nutrition for Health and Development, focuses on equity and implementation research. Dr. Kunal Bagchi, Regional Adviser for Nutrition and Food Safety at the WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia in New Delhi, India, provides expertise in regional nutrition strategies. Dr. Mercy Chikoko, Acting Regional Adviser for Nutrition at the WHO African Regional Office in Brazzaville, Congo, focuses on nutrition initiatives in the African region. Dr. Chessa Lutter, Regional Adviser for Child and Adolescent Health at the WHO Regional Office for the Americas/Pan American Health Organization in Washington, D.C., specializes in child health. Dr. Nancy Aburto, from the United Nations World Food Programme in Rome, Italy, contributes expertise in food security and nutrition. Professor Norm Campbell, based in Calgary, Canada, specializes in medicine, community health sciences, physiology, and pharmacology. Dr. Guillermo Carroli, from Centro Rosarino de Estudios Perinatales (CREP) in Santa Fé, Argentina, focuses on perinatal health. Ms. Nita Dalmiya, from the Micronutrients Unit at UNICEF in New York, specializes in micronutrient interventions. Dr. Maria Cecilia Dedios Sanguinetti, an independent consultant based in Baltimore, United States, provides expertise in nutrition and health. Dr. Kathryn Dewey, from the University of California, Davis, specializes in international and community nutrition. Ms. Mary-Anne Land, a Research Associate at The George Institute for Global Health in Sydney, Australia, focuses on global health research. Mr. Lorenzo Locatelli-Rossi, a Senior Technical Specialist at the Universal Salt Iodization Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN) in Geneva, Switzerland, specializes in salt iodization. Dr. Sant-Rayn Pasricha, from the MRC Human Immunology Unit at the University of Oxford, focuses on molecular medicine and immunology. Dr. Rafael Perez-Escamilla, from the Yale School of Public Health, specializes in community health and nutrition. Dr. Usha Ramakrishnan, from Emory University in Atlanta, United States, focuses on global health and nutrition sciences. Dr. Michael Zimmermann, from the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) in Zurich, specializes in food, nutrition, and health. Dr. Maria Andersson, also from ETH Zurich, contributes expertise in nutrition and health. Dr. Omar Dary, from the U.S. Agency for International Development in Washington, D.C., focuses on global health initiatives. Dr. Laurence Grummer-Strawn, from the CDC in Atlanta, specializes in nutrition, physical activity, and obesity prevention. Peer reviewers include Mr. Lorenzo Locatelli-Rossi, Mr. Arnold Timmer from UNICEF, and Dr. Michael Zimmermann. The WHO guideline on fortifying food-grade salt with iodine aims to prevent and control iodine deficiency disorders. It addresses questions on safety, target populations, and implementation strategies, considering factors such as salt consumption patterns and fortified salt sources. Outcomes include the prevention of goiter, hypothyroidism, and other iodine deficiency-related conditions across various age groups, including fetuses, neonates, children, and adults.
